title: Hosanna! Lord, Thine Angels Cry
description: Hosanna! Lord, Thine Angels Cry in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Reginald Heber wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 64 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Worship of Earth and Heaven”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ho-san-na! Lord, thine an-gels cry: Ho-san-na! Lord, we hear re-ply: A-bove, be-neath us, and a-round, The dead and liv-ing swell the sound.

lines: The dead and living swell the sound.
Meet us in this, thy house of prayer;
Thy promised blessing here we claim.
But, chiefest, in our cleansed breast,
And make our secret soul to be
A temple pure, and worthy thee.

licence: Public domain: Reginald Heber died in 1826.
credits: Words by Reginald Heber (1783–1826), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
